bib.title: Encouraging Divergent Thinking in Large Language Models through Multi-Agent Debate
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 2024 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (EMNLP), pages 17889-17904

question: Can a debate between LLM agents, managed by a judge, avoid the Degeneration-of-Thought problem of self-reflection and improve answers on tasks that need deep contemplation?
hypothesis: Because MAD lets other agents correct distorted thinking, offset rigidity and supply external feedback, it should be less susceptible to DoT than self-reflection and yield more accurate answers.
contributions: We propose and define the Degeneration-of-Thought (DoT) problem in self-reflection, and address it by proposing the Multi-Agent Debate (MAD) framework to explore divergent chain-of-thoughts.
Demonstrate MAD on two challenging tasks; GPT-3.5-Turbo with MAD can surpass GPT-4 on Common MT.
Adaptive break and a modest level of tit for tat are required for gains; the LLM judge prefers the side with the same LLM as backbone.

method.summary: Two debater agents (affirmative, negative) argue in turn from the shared debate history under a meta prompt that asks for tit for tat; a judge LLM either ends the debate (discriminative mode) or extracts the final answer after the iteration limit (extractive mode). Compared with Self-Reflect, Rerank, MAPS, CoT and Self-Consistency on GPT-3.5-Turbo and Vicuna.
method.task: Commonsense machine translation (zh to en) and counter-intuitive arithmetic reasoning; extra checks on GSM, AddSub and three BBH tasks

datasets.name: Common MT

datasets.name: Counter-Intuitive AR (CIAR)
datasets.source: Built by the authors from elicitation questions (Kong et al., 2022), web data (geeksforgeeks puzzles) and manual derivatives
datasets.preprocessing: Dataset explanations not used in experiments

datasets.name: GSM, AddSub, BBH Penguin/Date/Colored Objects

inference.samples: Rerank: 4 samples per item; Self-Consistency sample count not stated; MAD single run, number of runs/seeds not stated
inference.prompting: Zero-shot instructions, unified prompt asking for explanation and answer; question placed in <debate topic> of the meta prompt. CoT baseline appends 'Let's think step by step'.

other.agent_order: debaters speak one by one in fixed order based on history H

metrics.name: ACC
metrics.definition: accuracy of predictions on Counter-Intuitive AR

metrics.name: HUMAN
metrics.definition: direct assessment by three professional translators, scale 1 to 5, shuffled and anonymised, Krippendorff's Alpha 0.76

metrics.name: Bias
metrics.definition: human labels each sentence 1 (not conforming to commonsense) or 0; ambiguity error rate over test set

metrics.name: Diversity

metrics.name: Extra generated tokens
metrics.definition: generated tokens relative to CoT on Counter-Intuitive AR

eval.protocol: Single reported number per cell; no seeds, variance or significance tests stated. Human evaluation by 3 translators.

availability.data: Counter-Intuitive AR described; release not explicitly stated

prompts.text: You are a debater. Hello and welcome to the debate competition. It's not necessary to fully agree with each other's perspectives, as our objective is to find the correct answer. The debate topic is stated as follows: <debate topic>.
You are affirmative side. Please express your viewpoints.
You are negative side. You disagree with the affirmative side's points. Provide your reasons and answer.

You are a moderator. There will be two debaters involved in a debate competition. They will present their answers and discuss their perspectives on the <debate topic>. At the end of each round, you will evaluate both sides' answers and decide which one is correct.
What is the correct English translation of the following Chinese text
Both sides must reach a full consensus on every point of the debate. Every statement must be agreed upon by both sides.
Most of the debate should be characterized by disagreements, but there may still be a small amount of consensus on less significant points.
Both sides must disagree with each other on every point of the debate. There should be no consensus whatsoever.

evidence.quote: setting the maximum debate iteration to 3

results.claim: On Counter-Intuitive AR, MAD on GPT-3.5-Turbo reaches 37.0% accuracy, above CoT, Self-Consistency and Self-Reflect but below GPT-4.
results.setup: Counter-Intuitive AR, 200 questions, GPT-3.5-Turbo-0301, zero-shot, temperature 0; baseline is plain GPT-3.5-Turbo

results.claim: Other GPT-3.5-Turbo methods on Counter-Intuitive AR: CoT 28.0, Self-Consistency 29.5, Self-Reflect 27.5; GPT-4 51.0.
results.setup: Counter-Intuitive AR, Self-Consistency row; sample count not stated

results.claim: GPT-4 scores 51.0% on Counter-Intuitive AR, well above GPT-3.5-Turbo with MAD.
On Common MT lexical ambiguity, GPT-3.5-Turbo + MAD gets human score 3.78 vs GPT-4 3.41 and plain Turbo 3.14.
results.setup: Common MT lexical subset, 200 examples, 3 human translators; GPT-4 is 3.41
results.table: Table 1, row + MAD (Turbo), column Lexical HUMAN
results.note: Gap to GPT-4 is on lexical; on contextless 3.67 vs 3.63 and contextual 3.67 vs 3.65 the gap is small

results.claim: Contextless syntactic ambiguity: MAD on Turbo scores human 3.67 vs GPT-4 3.63.
results.setup: Common MT contextless subset, 450 examples; baseline is GPT-4
results.table: Table 1, row + MAD, column Contextless HUMAN

results.claim: Self-Reflect barely moves Turbo human score on lexical (3.43 vs 3.14) but MAD gets 3.78.
results.setup: Common MT lexical, GPT-3.5-Turbo + Self-Reflect; MAPS also 3.43
results.table: Table 1, row + Self-Reflect, column Lexical HUMAN

results.claim: MAD improves Vicuna-7b on lexical human score from 2.55 to 2.67 and Vicuna-13b from 2.81 to 2.96, small gains.
results.setup: Common MT lexical, Vicuna-13b-v1.5-16k; Vicuna-7b goes 2.55 to 2.67
results.table: Table 1, row Vicuna-13b + MAD, column Lexical HUMAN

results.claim: MAD cuts translation bias from 29.0 to 24.8 and raises diversity from 19.3 to 49.7 compared with Self-Reflect.
results.setup: Common MT, GPT-3.5-Turbo; Self-Reflect vs MAD; Bias is human-labelled error rate

results.claim: MAD costs 2.46 times the CoT generated tokens on Counter-Intuitive AR, versus 1.83 for Self-Reflect.
results.table: Table 12, row MAD, column Cost (# Generated Tokens)

results.setup: Common MT, GPT-3.5-Turbo debaters, 4 debaters vs default 2

results.setup: Common MT, Turbo as judge and both debaters
results.note: GPT-4 for all: 67 aff, 124 neg, 9 ties

results.claim: With mixed LLMs the judge prefers the side with its own backbone (GPT-4 judge, row 4: 120 vs 77, 3 ties).
results.setup: Common MT; row 4 is a GPT-4 vs Turbo debater pair; the table rows 3 and 4 give the judge/debater assignment ambiguously in the extracted text
results.note: Row 3: 52 aff, 136 neg, 12 ties. Which debater is which LLM is not recoverable from the cached text

results.claim: Strong debaters with a weak judge beat the reverse: Turbo debaters with Turbo judge get COMET 84.4 and human 3.69; with Vicuna-13b judge 83.2 and 3.47.
results.setup: Common MT, GPT-3.5-Turbo debaters; judge Turbo vs Vicuna-13b
results.table: Table 5, row GPT-3.5-Turbo as Debaters / GPT-3.5-Turbo judge, column COMET

results.note: Text: highest COMET score appears at the first iteration and is also lower than the result of the adaptive break

results.quote: "must disagree with each other on every point " (with a disagreement of 0.988)

results.claim: Self-reflection shows low disagreement between iterations, i.e. the LLM sticks to the CoT answer (DoT).
results.setup: 5 forced rounds, manual disagreement labels, Fig 1
results.note: Quote: The low disagreement of self-reflection suggests that the LLM sticks to the incorrect answers predicted by CoT

limits: Authors concede the method requires more time cost because agents interact over multiple rounds.
More than two debaters degraded results because LLMs forget other views and the judge struggles to extract from long text.
LLM judge may prefer outputs generated by itself; authors recommend same LLM for all roles or distinct LLMs for judge and debaters.
GPT-4 still beats MAD on Counter-Intuitive AR (51.0 vs 37.0).
No variance, seeds or significance tests; Self-Consistency sample count and model for Appendix C not stated.
Models are GPT-3.5-Turbo-0301, GPT-4-0314 and Vicuna v1.5 (dated); only two main tasks, one self-built 200-question set.
Compute-matched comparison with majority voting is not made: MAD uses 2.46x CoT tokens while Self-Consistency token cost is not reported.

terms.definition: Once the LLM-based agent has established confidence in its answers, it is unable to generate novel thoughts later through self-reflection even if the initial stance is incorrect.
The judge ends the debate early when it believes the correct solution has been obtained (discriminative mode).
Debaters are told to argue against each other, creating an atmosphere of debate.
